deck.title: A focused service model can reduce resolution time by 30%
deck.governingThought: Routing high-frequency cases to specialized teams can reduce resolution time while protecting service quality.

slides.actionTitle: A focused service model can reduce resolution time by 30%
slides.primaryClaim: The proposed model concentrates expertise on the cases that drive most delays.
slides.implication: The committee should evaluate the proposal as a speed-and-quality intervention.
slides.speakerNotes: Open with the decision required at the end of the meeting.

slides.actionTitle: Three operational shifts make a 90-day pilot both valuable and controllable
slides.primaryClaim: Specialization, routing rules, and weekly governance are the minimum viable pilot system.

evidence.claim: A small set of case types accounts for most avoidable delay.

slides.implication: Approve a bounded pilot rather than a broad transformation.
slides.speakerNotes: Replace illustrative evidence with validated client data before delivery.

slides.actionTitle: Two case categories account for most excess resolution time
slides.primaryClaim: Targeting the two largest delay contributors creates the highest-value starting point.

evidence.claim: Categories A and B contribute 64% of excess hours.

slides.implication: Limit the initial specialist teams to the two highest-impact categories.
slides.speakerNotes: State the sample definition and calculation method.
